thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Mostly Fall, Hit By Facebook's Premarket Dive

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Mostly Fall, Hit By Facebook's Premarket Dive
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Nasdaq is coming off a record close
U.S. stock-index futures pointed to a lower open on Thursday, with outsize losses in the Nasdaq as Facebook shares plummeted following its disappointing quarterly results.
Investors continued to monitor the second-quarter earnings season, which will see a huge number of companies report on Thursday, as well the status of trade talks between the U.S. and its major trading partners. However, Facebook's slide could spark broader caution, given the social-media giant is one of the bellwethers of the technology sector, which has fueled the overall market's advance thus far this year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-gains-in-2018-arent-just-a-tech-story-but-theyre-mostly-a-tech-story-2018-07-12).
What are the main benchmarks doing?
S&P 500 futures lost 6 points, or 0.2%, to 2,835, while those for the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 shed 64.5 points, or 0.9%, to 7,405.
Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average , , which doesn't have Facebook as one of its components, bucked the negative trend, rising by 33 points, or 0.1%, to 25,436.
On Wednesday, the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite all finished higher, with the Nasdaq closing at a record and the S&P exiting its longest correction since 1984 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-sp-500-just-ended-its-longest-stint-in-correction-territory-since-1984-2018-07-25). The indexes rallied into the close (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-in-holding-pattern-as-analysts-brace-for-trump-juncker-fireworks-2018-07-25) after President Donald Trump and European Union chief Jean-Claude Juncker made an announcement on trade that was received positively (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/after-trade-deal-trump-says-the-eu-and-us-obviously-love-each-other-2018-07-26).
Opinion:Even if short of specifics, the Trump-Juncker agreement is significant (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/even-if-short-of-specifics-the-trump-juncker-agreement-is-significant-2018-07-25)
The three gauges are showing year-to-date advances of 2.8% to 15%, as of Wednesday's close.
What's driving markets?
Facebook(FB)has been among the tech giants powering the stock market's gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-sector-contributed-all-of-the-stock-market-gains-so-far-in-2018-2018-07-02) this year, but the script just flipped. The social-media giant's shares were dropping 19% in premarket action after the company late Wednesday revealed lower-than-expected quarterly revenue, slowing user growth and weak guidance (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-stock-crushed-after-revenue-user-growth-miss-2018-07-25). Other so-called FAANG stocks--which refers to the quintet of large-capitalization technology and internet stocks, a group that many analysts frequently warn is overvalued--could also take a hit.
While Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL) posted strong results earlier this week (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alphabets-bets-promise-more-growth-ahead-analysts-applaud-tech-giants-results-2018-07-24), Netflix (NFLX)also disappointed this season (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-stock-slammed-after-second-quarter-subscriber-numbers-and-revenue-fall-short-2018-07-16). The dominance of FAANG stocks could be shakier following Facebook's comments.
Outside of Facebook-related gloom, European stocks on Thursday were cheering Wednesday's upbeat meeting between Trump and the European Commission's president. The two leaders reached a trade agreement that has been called short on specifics, but still significant. The deal shows the White House is willing to at least consider not letting global trade tensions spiral out of control, said a MarketWatch column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/even-if-short-of-specifics-the-trump-juncker-agreement-is-significant-2018-07-25).
What are strategists saying?
"Facebook is expected to see its biggest one-day selloff when it opens later today. The big question will be whether it will bring down the rest of the FAANG stocks," said Jasper Lawler, head of research at London Capital Group, in a note, referring to Facebook, Apple Inc.(AAPL), Amazon.com Inc.(AMZN), Netflix, and Alphabet.
"Whilst we expect Facebook's results have a short-term impact on FAANG stocks, it's more likely that we will start to see a de-coupling of Facebook from the group," Lawler added.
Which other stocks are in focus?
Comcast Corp. (CMCSA) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that came in ahead of forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/comcast-earnings-boosted-by-broadband-growth-2018-07-26), but lower-than-expected revenue.
Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) climbed 4.9% in premarket trading after the chip maker reported revenue that grew more than expected.
ConocoPhillips (COP) posted adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/concophillips-tops-eps-estimates-2018-07-26).
Raytheon Co. (RTN) gained 1.2% in premarket trading after the defense company reported second-quarter earnings and revenue that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/raytheon-shares-rise-after-q2-profit-revenue-beats-2018-07-26).
Dunkin' Brands Group Inc. (DNKN) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat analyst forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dunkin-brands-lowers-guidance-2018-07-26), but it lowered its outlook.
Under Armour Inc.(UAA) popped 5.4% before the bell after it posted stronger-than-expected second-quarter revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/under-armour-shares-rose-after-revenue-beat-estimates-2018-07-26).
PayPal Holdings Inc. (PYPL) gave a third-quarter outlook that missed expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/paypal-falls-after-outlook-miss-but-coo-says-investors-misunderstanding-the-forecast-2018-07-25). Shares fell 3% before the bell.
Which economic reports are on tap?
Three reports are slated to hit at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, covering weekly jobless claims, durable goods orders and advance trade in goods. For those three releases, economists polled by MarketWatch expect 219,000 claims, June growth of 3.7% and a June deficit of $67.3 billion, respectively.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
A second-quarter reading on housing vacancies is due to arrive at 10 a.m. Eastern.
What are other markets doing?
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/germanys-dax-jumps-15-after-eu-us-trade-truce-leading-european-higher-2018-07-26)traded higher after the U.S.-EU trade truce, while Asian markets finished mixed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-as-eisei-weighs-down-nikkei-2018-07-25).
Gold futures and oil futures were lower, as the ICE U.S. Dollar Index also lost ground.
